Introduction

From internet radio to social media radio

  • Internet radio added live audio, scheduling, and global reach to broadcasting
  • Social platforms added algorithmic recommendation, audience metrics, and social circulation
  • Social media radio = programmed live voice + platform logic + public-service expectations
  • Egyptian context: university radio traditions, digital media literacy gaps, misinformation pressure
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 20263 / 36

Introduction

Why a radio-specific case, not generic social media

  • Radio-like audio is voice-centered and temporally organized: a programmed stream, not an undifferentiated feed
  • Broadcaster identity, vocal presence, sequence, and repair are directly observable
  • Engagement has a behavioral referent: continued listening, replay, interaction
  • Editorial, platform, and listener selection can be separated and varied as distinct levers
  • Analytical generalization: the mechanism, not the medium, is the inferential target
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 20264 / 36

Introduction

Statement of the problem

  • Platform design, audience measurement, and epistemic quality live in separate literatures
  • Filter bubbles, misinformation diffusion, and engagement pressure are studied without a measurable audience rating
  • No existing framework links platform architecture to how students judge what they hear
  • Question: can a social media radio design improve epistemic judgment without losing the audience?
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 20265 / 36

Introduction

Importance of the study

  • Joins platform design, audience measurement, and epistemic quality in one falsifiable framework (EST)
  • Makes the core trade-off measurable: epistemic gain vs engagement cost
  • Speaks to the Egyptian university media context with a public-service language for social audio
  • Delivers a specified, testable design (LOKLOK) plus a plan for a real deployment
  • Every claim is tiered and model-conditional: honesty as scientific practice
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 20266 / 36

Introduction

Aim of the study

  • To propose Epistemic Systems Theory and the LOKLOK platform, and to test, with a calibrated in-silico experiment anchored in a measured student wave, whether the epistemic-first design raises evaluative and competence-format ratings without destroying engagement
  • The measured wave anchors the model; the simulation tests what the specified design implies
  • No live trial was possible; no field causal effect is claimed
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 20267 / 36

Introduction

Objectives

  • Synthesize the literature into EST with four testable propositions
  • Specify the LOKLOK architecture (BRS, MORE, ERIC, cooling, attention gate, measurement surface)
  • Collect and analyze a measured wave of university students to anchor the model
  • Build a reproducible calibrated in-silico experiment (500 personas, 8 cells, 18 sessions)
  • Validate the qualitative codebook and apply the pre-set machine-coding gate
  • Triangulate the contrast across four assignment designs
  • Derive design implications and a plan for a real deployment

Hypotheses

  • H3 Psychometric validity: instruments meet psychometric accountability (EST-P3)

Framework

Epistemic Systems Theory (EST)

  • EST-P1 Architecture is a structural condition of credibility
  • EST-P2 Diversity and cooling constrain epistemic concentration
  • EST-P3 Measurement is an accountability requirement
  • EST-P4 Participation and evidence-based production are the educational test
  • A falsifiable language for linking design choices to audience judgment, not a universal law
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202611 / 36

Platform

LOKLOK: six design components

  • BRS Broadcaster Reputation Score
  • MORE Recommendations constrained to keep viewpoints varied
  • ERIC Moderation loop: reflect, invite, correct
  • Echo Meter and Algorithmic Cooling
  • Zewail-inspired attention gate (time-resolved attentional coherence)
  • Built-in measurement surface: evaluative and competence-format student ratings
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202612 / 36

Methodology

Three evidence layers, one honest hierarchy

  • Measured 52 of 60 questionnaires, Uber riders in 6th of October City: anchors, not a causal test
  • Qualitative FGD and self-report, 193 segments, 3 human coders: an assumption audit
  • Modeling A calibrated in-silico experiment: what the specified design implies
  • Mixed-methods integration through claim tiers: field, model, theory, prospective
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202613 / 36

Methodology

Participants and instruments

  • Participants: 60 questionnaires collected; 8 duplicate vectors removed; N = 52 university students using Uber in 6th of October City, Giza
  • BRS: 11-item broadcaster-rating battery (alpha .957)
  • PB: 5-item perceived-benefit battery (alpha .947, omega .962)
  • Star rating, ride duration, interaction level, and context items
  • NMLS: published 35-item media-literacy profile scored with GRM-IRT; 8-item MCS+PB battery
  • Convenience sample: descriptive anchoring, not population inference
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202614 / 36

Methodology

The measured wave in one slide

  • Perceived benefit: M = 5.12, SD = 0.87 on a 7-point scale
  • PB correlates with the star rating: rho = .67
  • Reliability is high (alpha .957 and .947); the single-factor CFA fits poorly
  • Therefore: reliability is reported, structural validity is not claimed
  • The wave anchors the model level (G0 = 5.119) and the persona spread
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202615 / 36

Methodology

Qualitative corpus and coding design

  • FGD 160 segments; self-report 185 segments; 60 participant-observation accounts; 4,828 corpus documents
  • 25-code codebook: 12 deductive mechanism codes (C01-C12), 13 inductive codes (I01-I13)
  • Three independent human coders on 193 usable segments
  • Machine comparators: local Qwen 7B (zero-shot and gold 5-fold) and a Claude first pass
  • Pre-set usability gate: 8 positives, kappa at least .60, at most 5% fabrication
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202616 / 36

Qualitative validation

An honest null result

  • Human agreement: pooled pairwise kappa .762, .852, .861; per-code median .28 (C02) to .95 (I07)
  • Leave-one-out human micro-F1 about .99 (97% of code cells are negative)
  • Qwen 7B: micro-F1 .193 zero-shot, .320 with gold exemplars; Claude first pass .452
  • No mechanism code met the gate in either local pass
  • The qualitative layer remains an assumption audit; E1 and E2 exploratory, E3 not run
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202617 / 36

Method

The calibrated in-silico experiment

  • 500 synthetic personas drawn from the debiased distribution of the 52 respondents (DML + IPW, spectral manifold)
  • 8 cells (2³ A/B/C combinations), 18 sessions, eight mathematical filters
  • GRM-IRT measurement: 35-item NMLS competence profile, 8-item MCS+PB battery
  • G0 arm anchored to the measured PB mean (5.119)
  • State-outcome weights are declared design assumptions, not estimates
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202618 / 36

Decomposition

What drives the contrast

  • B (diversity and cooling) carries most of it: main effect +0.6265
  • A (BRS) adds +0.1905; C (ERIC) is near zero alone (-0.0121)
  • B x C interaction +0.3791: nearly half of the total contrast
  • 256-point joint sweep: 96.5% positive, median +0.567, range -0.244 to +1.810
  • Top driver: the declared diversity-to-credibility weight (PRCC +0.77)
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202624 / 36

Trade-off

The epistemic gain is not free

Pareto panel: no cell dominates G1 on both epistemic rating and engagement. The Hamiltonian is a specification diagnostic, not a physical law.

LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202626 / 36

Robustness

Controls, stress tests, and topologies

  • Placebo factor D (absent from the equations): -0.003 SR eval, -0.082 SR comp
  • Pre-treatment negative controls: +0.001, -0.008, 0.000 across the A/B/C margins
  • Mechanism checks: B raises chosen diversity +1.299; A raises BRS +0.019; B x C lowers echo -0.340
  • Adversarial content stress (poor-content share 0.763): contrast +0.636, still positive
  • 60-row sensitivity +0.808; 50 anchor bootstraps +0.839 (100% positive); ER/WS/BA topologies +0.827/+0.826/+0.832
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202627 / 36

Triangulation

Gemini persona-agent pilot

Gemini reproduces the direction but overstates the magnitude (+2.650) and reverses engagement (+0.163). Single-shot appraisal, not an 18-session simulation.

Answers

Answering the research questions

  • RQ1 architecture: partial support; measured associations plus the model BRS path; model-conditional
  • RQ2 diversity and cooling: supported within the model; the topology check is network-independent
  • RQ3 psychometrics: mixed; reliability high, structural validity not established
  • RQ4 integration: not established; the constructs remain framework-level
  • RQ5 drivers: cred_dbi +0.77, cred_brs +0.31, cred_echo -0.27; B main +0.6265
  • RQ6 Gemini: direction only; magnitude and engagement sign are not reproduced
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202629 / 36

Answers

Hypothesis results

  • H1 structural credibility: partial (model-conditional)
  • H2 diversity mechanism: supported within the model
  • H3 psychometric validity: mixed
  • H4 integration: not established
  • H5 conformity and H6 scheduling: exploratory; no confirmatory claim
  • H7 participatory performance: prospective; untested

Boundaries

What is deliberately not claimed

  • No randomized field deployment; convenience sample; no causal claim
  • Model weights are declared assumptions; the Bayesian check is a re-expression, not independent evidence
  • No human NMLS validation; measurement invariance not estimated
  • BRS is not validated as a consequential ranking instrument
  • The engagement metric differs by convention: -0.183 session-average, -0.217 terminal; both reported
LOKLOK | Master's Defense | November 202632 / 36

Contribution

What this thesis contributes

  • EST: a falsifiable framework linking architecture, audience judgment, and measurement
  • LOKLOK: a specified, testable platform design
  • A reproducible calibrated in-silico experiment plus a plan for a real deployment
  • A transparent reporting standard: assumption audit, claim tiers, and a pre-set machine-coding gate

Future work

From model to field

  • Prospective platform experiment with frozen allocations and disclosed LLM-agent logs
  • Longitudinal human NMLS validation and measurement invariance
  • E3: respondent-level theme features vs BGE-PCA (requires the provenance pass)

Defense readiness

Three numbers, four expected questions

  • Three numbers to remember: +0.827, -0.183, 96.5%
  • Is this just MORE? Yes: diversity-seeking selection plus a declared credibility weight is the design claim
  • Shuffled text gives the same answer? The data set the level and persona spread, not the contrast
  • Why does the default sit at the 78th percentile of the sweep? Declared design values; the sweep brackets them
  • Why is the baseline gate open only about 15% of the time? A strong attentional filter; the dephasing time is an assumption
